added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13- and 52-week repeat-dose toxicity (necrotic dermatosis at the extremities, the DPP-8/9-linked cutaneous toxicity of the gliptin class)

safety.confidence_note: Read from the English PMDA review (3.(iii).A.(2).5)-(2).6), pdftotext); the study reports 4.2.3.2-7/-8 are not public. The review is dated 2012-04-05; the application was filed 2011-08-26.
safety.note: Teneligliptin 75-100 mg/kg/day gave necrotic dermatosis of auricle and tail in cynomolgus monkeys (13- and 52-week studies); NOAEL 30 mg/kg/day, 13-25x clinical AUC.
safety.quote: One male and 2 females in the 75 mg/kg/day showed necrotic dermatosis in the auricle, tail, etc., and in these animals, teneligliptin was withdrawn or administered in reduced dose from Day 40.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. Its own track: the draft's animal-tox-package track is rat, dog and mouse on a prusogliptin paper and names no monkey and no harm; this is a named species-specific finding with its own mechanism literature (DPP-8/9 inhibition, Lankas 2005 rat/dog syndrome cited via the Januvia package).

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted harm (necrotic dermatosis) vs its incidence in the Japanese and foreign teneligliptin trials: none
safety.confidence_note: Tier 2, English review text. The same review's 3.(iii).B.(3) concludes the skin toxicity 'is most likely to be unique only to monkeys' and PMDA accepted it; the package insert still cautions that it was seen in monkeys.
safety.note: No necrotic dermatosis or serious skin reaction in any teneligliptin trial; applicant and PMDA call the monkey skin toxicity species-specific (DPP-8/9 class finding).
safety.short: Monkey skin harm absent in patients
safety.quote: Necrotic dermatosis observed in the oral toxicity study in monkeys and serious hypersensitivity reactions observed with drugs of the same class were not observed in any of the clinical studies.
safety.reason: Predicted skin necrosis never appeared in patients
safety.judgement: Decision 5 canonical case: the regulator itself calls the predicted harm species-specific, so contra with magnitude opposite. product_in_model true because teneligliptin was dosed; the vildagliptin/saxagliptin monkey data and the Januvia DPP-8/9 package are the mechanism source only. Not changed by later labels: pemphigoid entered the teneligliptin (2016-11-22) and omarigliptin (2018-04-19) labels, a different pathology the monkeys did not show (checker rule question 2), and omarigliptin's 3-month monkey study (9 mg/kg/day, 48x AUC) was silent on skin with no necrotic dermatosis in its trials, a same that cannot turn a contra track back. The checker proposed correcting the draft's animal-tox-package 2021 entry from this same finding; the merger should carry it on one track only.

added_models.model: hERG channel assay plus dog and monkey ECG/telemetry (QTc) safety pharmacology

safety.confidence_note: English review 3.(i).A.(3).2) and 3.(i).B.(2), pdftotext; the quote is PMDA's own summary of the package (hERG IC50 3.45 uM, guinea-pig papillary muscle APD NOEL 4x, monkey and dog QTc prolongation).
safety.note: Teneligliptin hERG IC50 3.45 uM (15x unbound Cmax at 40 mg); monkey QTc prolongation at 30 mg/kg, NOEL 10 mg/kg (17x); dog 7 mg/kg i.v.
safety.quote: In vitro and in vivo studies on teneligliptin show effects suggestive of QTc interval prolongation.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Its own track: a safety-pharmacology system (ion channel plus non-rodent ECG), distinct from the draft's in-silico C-QTc track and from the generic rat/dog/mouse tox track.

safety.magnitude_basis: exposure multiple of the 40 mg unbound Cmax at which QTc prolongation appears: model NOEL 17x (monkey) and hERG IC50 15x vs the 160 mg thorough-QT arm at about 4.5x the 40 mg Cmax (2259 vs 499.7 ng/mL)
safety.confidence_note: Tier 2; the applicant's response in 3.(i).B.(2) puts the hERG/monkey/dog data and the thorough-QT result in one paragraph, and PMDA's 4.(iii).B.(3).7) attributes the human QTc prolongation to hERG inhibition by the parent drug. Thorough-QT study MP-513-A01 has no registry record found; dates are redacted in the review.
safety.note: Thorough QT (MP-513-A01): ddQTcI 9.3 [5.6, 13.0] ms at 160 mg near tmax, 3.9 [0.2, 7.6] ms at 40 mg; PMDA ties it to hERG.
safety.short: QTc rose at 160 mg as hERG predicted
safety.quote: In addition, in the Thorough QT/QTc study, QTc interval prolongation was observed only time points near tmax after administration of teneligliptin 160 mg, and no clinically significant QTc interval prolongation was observed at 40 mg
safety.judgement: Predicted harm appeared, at a supratherapeutic dose: same in direction, margin about 4x narrower than the animal NOEL. Counted once, here in safety; no dose-ceiling entry is made on this track (decision 16, checker rule question 3), and the 40 mg maximum dose was clean, so the Japanese label carries a QT caution rather than a dose restriction.

safety.magnitude_basis: QTc risk at clinical exposure: no effect predicted below 40.8x unbound Cmax (dog telemetry NOEL) and 76.9x (hERG IC20); the thorough-QT at 7x the clinical dose gave max ddQTcP 3.66 ms; the human multiple is not given on the unbound basis
safety.confidence_note: Japanese review read via pdftotext (nonclinical 2) 心血管系 and clinical (6) QT/QTc 評価試験 P010); the quote is the contiguous span of the TQT sentence after the footnote marker 52 ('心電図について、第 1 日目に本薬 25 mg、第 2 日目に本薬 175 mg を投与したときの QTcP 間隔 ...'), and the sentence continues 'msec であり、信頼区間の上限が 10 msec を下回った'. comparison_stated false because the review states the animal margins against clinical Cmax but does not itself set them beside the thorough-QT result; model side is the same document. P010 has no registry record found.
safety.note: Omarigliptin hERG IC50 105 uM; dog telemetry QT/QTc up only at 75 mg/kg (NOEL 40.8x); thorough QT 175 mg: ddQTcP 3.66 ms.
safety.quote: ベースラインからの変化量のプラセボ群との差の最大値とその 90%信頼区間は 3.66［1.56, 5.76］
safety.reason: Animal QT margins held in thorough-QT studies
safety.judgement: Second member, status unchanged: the model predicted no QTc liability at clinical exposure with a stated 40.8x margin, and the thorough-QT at 175 mg (7x the 25 mg dose) showed no clinically relevant prolongation. The draft credits omarigliptin's QT only to the in-silico C-QTc model (Krishna 2016); the filed basis was this animal package.

added_models.model: Dog and monkey pharmacokinetics scaled allometrically to a human half-life and dosing interval (once-weekly omarigliptin, biweekly cofrogliptin)

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the ACS full text with the animal half-lives and the allometric projection could not be opened. Merck authors. model_filed true because the 2015 Marizev review carries the rat and dog PK.
dose.note: Omarigliptin's rat, dog and monkey PK projected a human half-life long enough for once-weekly dosing; no human regimen yet compared.
dose.quote: MK-3102 (omarigliptin), was identified as a potent and selective dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor with an excellent pharmacokinetic profile amenable for once-weekly human dosing and selected as a clinical development candidate.
dose.judgement: Own track per the checker: the regimen prediction comes from non-rodent PK scaled to humans, not from the rodent plasma-DPP-4/OGTT system that the draft's dose index 3 (Krishna 2016) is keyed to. Dose only: the system predicts exposure and interval, not efficacy or harm.

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: once-weekly projected from dog/monkey PK vs once-weekly at 25 mg holding 87.5% trough DPP-4 inhibition at 168 h in Japanese healthy adults (P005) and HbA1c superiority at 24 weeks (P020)
dose.confidence_note: Japanese review read via pdftotext; the applicant's dose rationale (審査の概略, 本薬の効果について and (6) 用法・用量) sets rat MRT ~11 h and dog t1/2 ~22 h beside the human alpha 33-50 h / beta ~140 h half-lives and the 87.5% trough inhibition; the allometric step itself is stated in Biftu 2014, not in the review. No tolerated-dose ceiling is stated by the allometry, so margin_stated stays null.
dose.note: Human alpha t1/2 33-50 h, beta ~140 h beside dog 22 h; 25 mg weekly held 87.5% trough DPP-4 inhibition, weekly regimen stood.
dose.short: Weekly interval from animal PK held
dose.quote: 日本人健康成人に本薬 25 mg を週 1 回 3 週間反復経口投与したときの最終投与 168 時間後における本薬未変化体の血漿中非結合形薬物濃度は 8.2 nmol/L、血漿中 DPP-4 活性阻害率は 87.5%であった（P005 試験）。
dose.judgement: The predicted regimen (weekly) was reached and was enough: trough DPP-4 inhibition above the 80% target and a positive 24-week Phase 3 at that interval. The draft's dose index 3 (Krishna 2016, tier 1) is this comparison on the wrong track; it should be re-keyed to this model_id rather than duplicated, so no 2016 entry is added here.

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: monkey DPP-4 inhibition ~80% through day 14 after 10 mg/kg plus allometric scaling vs the biweekly 10/25 mg regimen that lowered HbA1c 0.63/0.59% at week 24 (NCT04556851)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, open access; sponsor (Haisco) authors. Published 2026-01-05, after the Phase 3 (Gao 2025, doi:10.1111/dom.16014; NCT04556851, no results posted) read out. The monkey work is IND-enabling pharmacology run before the clinic, so scored prospective (retrodiction false) and dated at publication (decision 7); this is the checker's rule question 4, and if read as a retrodiction the status becomes retro. model_filed null: the Chinese NMPA review is not public.
dose.note: Cofrogliptin 10 mg/kg held ~80% monkey DPP-4 inhibition through day 14; allometry predicted the biweekly regimen that lowered HbA1c in Phase 3.
dose.quote: Based on allometric scaling analyses, cofrogliptin is predicted to display superior human pharmacokinetic properties relative to MK3102, with anticipated longer-acting features that align with its clinical dosing frequency.
dose.reason: Animal PK set the interval that held
dose.judgement: Second member on the track, status unchanged. The draft dropped this because the paper post-dates the Phase 3; v3 dates by public date, so it is entered as strengthens with the retrodiction question flagged rather than left out.

considered_not_added: Rodent plasma DPP-4 / OGTT data in both PMDA reviews (Wistar ED50, Zucker carbohydrate load, Phase 2/3 HbA1c beside them, monkey NOAEL as the dose-ceiling margin): existing rodent-dpp4-ogtt track; the checker's corrections (model_filed true, year 2012, margin_stated true) apply there, not a new system.

Prusogliptin patient PK/PD 2025 (Liu, Clin Pharmacokinet 10.1007/s40262-025-01501-8, 62-89% DPP-4 inhibition, NCT05146869) with Yeh 2021 as model side: an engagement entry on the existing rodent-dpp4-ogtt track.
Krishna 2016 once-weekly PK/PD in healthy subjects (draft dose index 3): the same comparison as the new nonrodent-pk-allometry track; left for the merger to re-key rather than duplicated.

Lankas 2005 rat/dog DPP-8/9 toxicity syndrome (Januvia package, doi:10.2337/diabetes.54.10.2988): the selectivity model every member was designed against, but no member was dosed in it and its comparison is with sitagliptin-era data (non-member); cited as mechanism source on the cyno-repeat-dose-skin-tox track only.

Rat lung phospholipidosis (foamy alveolar macrophages, ~20x margin, teneligliptin review 3.(iii).B.(2)) vs the 2014-10-21 interstitial pneumonia label addition (6 cases): different pathology, no source pairs them, and the rat finding sits on the draft's generic animal-tox-package track; a drafter pairing would be low-confidence speculation.

Pemphigoid label additions (teneligliptin 2016-11-22, omarigliptin 2018-04-19): patient-side harms on which the monkey and dog studies were silent; whether an autoimmune blistering disease is a harm the species could have shown is the checker's rule question 2, so recorded in the cyno track judgement, not as a status change.

Omarigliptin 3-month monkey / 9-month dog studies silent on skin and eye (48x and 788x AUC) with no necrotic dermatosis in its trials: a same on the cyno-repeat-dose-skin-tox track, but a later same cannot turn a contra track back (v3 status rules), so not entered.

Cofrogliptin PBPK for special populations (Ejps 2023, 10.1016/j.ejps.2023.106553) and teneligliptin age PBPK (Diabetes Ther 2024): human-data in-silico dose tools; same scope question as the draft's PopPK/PD and C-QTc tracks (checker rule question 1) and no verified comparison of a prediction with a later patient result.
Omarigliptin concentration-QTc model and cofrogliptin PopPK/PD-MBMA: already tracks in the draft.
Patient-derived cells/organoids, PDX, ex-vivo sensitivity, human challenge and DPP4 loss-of-function genetics: searched, nothing comparing a member with patients found.
